Its been a month or so now so lets talk about this book. What are your thoughts?

I am a bit confused by how anyone could think it was a good idea to leave the rock and go to a higher orbit with no plans to do anything after that.

So, first off, I didn't "read" this as much as listen to the audio version. I want to preface is with that because I didn't really enjoy the last part as much as the first, but that may also be due to the change in narrator. I felt like there were two different stories. The first part seemed like a history setting up the second part....only the setup had better characters.

That said, I did enjoy the book overall. I thought it was a nice new spin on how the world ends, and I really enjoyed the way the characters progressed from Ohhh look at that, there are seven moons, to Oh fuck we're all dead.

I think the higher orbit DID make sense for a few reasons. Our narrators for the most part of set up in the ISS. They have a giant rock blocking incoming bolides and other debris. The rest of the cloud ark however, the part we never really talk to, isn't nearly as well protected. They want to get somewhere safe. Our narrators have a plan...at least we think they do. We have hints at what's coming about moving into Kidney Bean and they're constantly plotting and planning. The members of the Cloud Ark...well they don't have this insight. For all they know they're sitting in dirty space with no plan. Finally, there's Mars. The people most responsible for the Big Ride also sent a mission to Mars. We never hear back from it, but part of their plan (however poor a plan it was) was to move higher into orbit, and eventually go to Mars. As a side note, there's also the fuel issue. I THINK that higher orbits take less fuel to maintain...but the fuel/propulsion issue was one that I never really figured out so it may be moot. So yeah, it makes some sense to me why they'd go. Not if you have all the information we have as the reader, but if you can think about the knowledge gap that existed I think it will make more sense. Maybe still not the idea you'd have gone with, but at least not crazy.
